prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour Party Manifesto 2024 — Summary (under 500 words)

Core aim: “National renewal” focused on working people, economic stability, and long‑term, mission‑driven government. Immediate “first steps”: restore stability; cut NHS waits (40,000 extra weekly appointments); launch a Border Security Command; set up publicly owned Great British Energy; crack down on antisocial behaviour; recruit 6,500 teachers.

Five national missions
- Highest sustained growth in the G7
- Clean power by 2030
- Halve serious violent crime; rebuild confidence in policing/justice
- Break down barriers to opportunity (childcare, schools, skills)
- Build an NHS fit for the future

Strong foundations
- National security: unshakeable NATO and nuclear deterrent; Strategic Defence Review; path to 2.5% of GDP on defence; counter state threats, cyber and extremism; Martyn’s Law.
- Secure borders: Border Security Command; EU security cooperation; more caseworkers to clear backlog and end hotel use; faster returns; enforcement unit; act upstream on crises.
- Economic stability: strict fiscal rules (current budget balance; debt falling by year 5); full OBR oversight; no austerity. No rises to National Insurance, basic/higher/additional Income Tax rates or VAT. Tackle avoidance; abolish non‑dom status; end carried interest loophole; modernise HMRC.

Kickstarting growth
- Industrial strategy with a statutory council; back UK strengths (R&D, advanced manufacturing, creative and financial services).
- National Wealth Fund (£7.3bn) to crowd in private capital for ports, gigafactories, green steel, CCUS, hydrogen.
- Business certainty: one major fiscal event a year; corporation tax capped at 25% for the Parliament; permanent full expensing; reform business rates.
- Infrastructure: 10‑year strategy; new National Infrastructure and Service Transformation Authority; planning reform for nationally significant projects and labs/datacentres; 5G/gigabit by 2030.
- Transport: maintain roads; fix 1m extra potholes/year; accelerate EV charging; 2030 ICE phase‑out restored; rail brought into public ownership as contracts end; bus franchising and municipal ownership enabled; integrated city transport.
- Innovation: 10‑year R&D budgets; National Data Library; Regulatory Innovation Office; binding rules for frontier AI; ban sexual deepfakes.
- SMEs/self‑employed: tackle late payments; improve export and procurement access; reform British Business Bank; strengthen Post Office; deliver Horizon justice.
- Housing: 1.5m homes; restore mandatory targets; brownfield‑first plus strategic “grey belt” release; new towns; more social/affordable homes; reform compulsory purchase; first‑time buyer preference; permanent mortgage guarantee.
- Devolution: landmark English devolution; Local Growth Plans; multi‑year council settlements; end competitive bidding.
- Immigration and work: reduce net migration; link skills and visas; enforce against abuse; youth guarantee (18–21); reform Jobcentres; New Deal for Working People (ban exploitative zero‑hours; end fire‑and‑rehire; day‑one rights; single enforcement body); minimum wage to reflect living costs and remove age bands.

Clean energy and nature
- Clean power by 2030: double onshore wind, triple solar, quadruple offshore wind; invest in CCUS, hydrogen, storage; expand nuclear (Hinkley, Sizewell, SMRs); retain gas strategic reserve; no new North Sea exploration licences; no fracking; tighten windfall tax.
- Great British Energy (£8.3bn), headquartered in Scotland, to co‑invest and scale local power projects.
- Warm Homes Plan: +£6.6bn for insulation/low‑carbon heating; PRS standards by 2030.
- Nature/water: enforce on polluting water companies (fines, bonus blocks, criminal charges); expand habitats; circular economy; support British farmers (public procurement targets, land‑use framework); animal welfare reforms (ban trail hunting, trophy imports, puppy smuggling, snares).

Crime and justice
- Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee; Respect Orders; specific offence for assaults on shopworkers; knife crime plan with mandatory interventions and bans on zombie/ninja blades; Young Futures hubs nationwide; specialist rape units and courts; spiking offence; stronger stalking protections; police vetting/standards overhaul; fraud strategy; expand charging capacity; build prison places; reduce reoffending; probation review; Hillsborough Law.

Opportunity and services
- Early years: 3,000 school‑based nurseries; parental leave review.
- Schools: 6,500 teachers; free primary breakfast clubs; curriculum/assessment review; mental health staff in every school; SEND inclusion; reform Ofsted reporting.
- Skills/HE: Skills England; Technical Excellence Colleges; flexible Growth & Skills Levy; HE funding reform and access.
- NHS/social care: 2m extra appointments/year; double CT/MRI scanners; New Hospitals Programme; modernised app; family doctor continuity; pharmacist prescribing; Dentistry Rescue Plan; National Care Service with Fair Pay Agreement; 8,500 more mental health staff and youth hubs; public health (smoking generation ban, restrict child‑targeted vapes, junk‑food ads, energy drinks).

Politics and foreign policy
- Ethics and Integrity Commission; ban MPs’ paid advisory roles; Commons modernisation.
- Lords reform now (end hereditaries, retirement at 80) and consult on replacement chamber.
- Votes at 16; reset with devolved governments.
- Foreign policy: steadfast on Ukraine; defence industrial strategy; AUKUS; calibrated China approach; make Brexit work (no SM/CU/FoM) with better EU trade/security ties; targeted trade deals (incl. India); Clean Power Alliance; rebuild development, restore 0.7% when fiscal space allows.
